Uncertified DAG consensus, machine-checked

Protocols, properties and mechanisms, formalised in Lean 4
The development is in Lean 4 over Mathlib. Every theorem named in the deck is checked by the Lean kernel. Whether the definitions say what the papers mean is checked by human and LLM review only; the README's provenance note applies. Background figure: witness Ugrow 5 (LeanDagTest/Mysticeti/Growth.lean).
Part I

Foundations

Scope

  • Protocols. Thirteen commit rules from the literature. Eleven are proved safe and live; two are shown unsafe or not live by counterexamples.
  • Properties. One small interface — four properties and a “support” — that each of the eleven rules is proved to satisfy.
  • Mechanisms. A pacemaker, chain quality, a storage bound, garbage collection, crash recovery, adaptive leaders and an adaptive leader count, checkpoints: each proved once against the interface, and composable.
  • Safety theorems use no assumption about the network.
  • The eleven rules with a carrier (DagRule): mysticetiRule (LeanDag/Mysticeti/Properties.lean:52), nemoRule (LeanDag/Nemo/Carrier.lean:37), odontocetiRule (LeanDag/Odontoceti/Carrier.lean:32), hybridRule (LeanDag/Hybrid/Carrier.lean:29), finWhaleRule (LeanDag/FinWhale/Carrier.lean:39), Hydrozoan.rule (LeanDag/Hydrozoan/Helpers/Carrier.lean:27), optimalRule (LeanDag/OptimalHydrozoan/Carrier.lean:42), bluestreakRule (LeanDag/Bluestreak/Carrier.lean:35), mahiMahiRule (LeanDag/MahiMahi/Carrier.lean:28), asyncBlueBottleRule (LeanDag/AsyncBlueBottle/Carrier.lean:26), steelheadRule (LeanDag/Steelhead/Properties.lean:41).
  • The two refuted rules: LeanDagTest/Minnow/Safety.lean, LeanDagTest/BlackMarlin/Divergence.lean.
  • Safety without network hypotheses: Properties.Safe (LeanDag/Properties/Arcs/Headline.lean:46), AnchoredRule.decided_agree (LeanDag/Common/Anchored.lean:483).
  • “Live” means progress for all eleven; four of them do not prove inclusion (slide 64).

The problem: replicated agreement

  • n validators each keep a copy of one ordered log (a ledger).
  • Clients submit transactions to any validator.
  • Safety: no two validators output conflicting logs.
  • Liveness: every transaction from a correct client is eventually in every correct validator’s log.
  • Some validators may be faulty. The protocol must tolerate them without identifying them.
(informal) Background for the audience. In Lean the ledger is commitSeq and ledgerSet (LeanDag/Common/Ledger.lean), and agreement of ledgers is AnchoredRule.commitSeq_agree, ledgerSet_agree (LeanDag/Common/Anchored.lean:521, 528).

Faults and quorums

  • A Byzantine validator may deviate arbitrarily from the protocol: send false messages, send none, or send different messages to different validators (equivocate).
  • A crashed validator stops and never resumes.
  • With n ≥ 3f + 1 validators, at most f Byzantine, a quorum is n − f validators.
  • Two quorums share at least n − 2f ≥ f + 1 validators, so at least one correct validator.
  • A correct validator does not equivocate, so two quorums cannot support two conflicting statements.
  • Faults (LeanDag/Common/Validators.lean:23): 3 * f + 1 ≤ n, byzantine.card ≤ f. Quorum quorumCard = n − f (Validators.lean:39).
  • Intersection: exists_correct_mem_inter (LeanDag/Common/Validators.lean:152).
  • Correct is the complement of byzantine; a crashed validator is in Correct. Liveness theorems name the validators that keep producing separately.

What the network is assumed to do

  • Messages can be delayed arbitrarily, up to an unknown time GST (global stabilisation time).
  • A reliable validator is a correct one that keeps producing blocks. Liveness assumes a quorum of them.
  • After GST, what one reliable validator holds reaches every reliable validator within Δ. This is called view convergence.
  • Safety is proved with no assumption about the network.
  • Liveness is proved from view convergence and the protocol’s own rules.
  • (informal) Partial synchrony is background.
  • View convergence: ConvergesWithin (LeanDag/Mysticeti/ViewPace.lean:61); PaceCore.converges (ViewPace.lean:166): gst ≤ t → holds w t ⊆ holds v (t + delay) for v, w ∈ T. T is a quorum-sized reliable set.
  • ViewPace also carries protocol rules (P7, P9), which are the validators’ behaviour, not the network.

Blocks and the DAG

  • Validators work in rounds. In each round each validator creates one block: a round number, its creator, references to earlier blocks, and a payload of transactions.
  • A valid block at round r > 0 references blocks of round r − 1 from at least n − f distinct creators, one of them its own creator.
  • The blocks and references form a directed acyclic graph (DAG). A block’s history is every block it reaches by references. A validator’s view is the set of blocks it holds, including their histories.
  • Blocks are named by identifier (a hash), so two validators may hold different sets of blocks but agree on what each identifier means.
  • Block (LeanDag/Common/Block.lean:20); ValidWrt (Block.lean:61) has four clauses: predecessor (references at r − 1), distinct creators, quorum, self-parent (some block by the creator).
  • Identifiers: BlockRecord.block (LeanDag/Common/BlockRecord.lean:35).
  • History: Reaches, historyFrom (LeanDag/Common/CausalHistory.lean, LeanDag/Common/History.lean). A view is closed under references (viewComplete, LeanDag/Properties/Carrier.lean:49).
  • Some rules change validity: Nemo drops self-parent and distinct creators and uses a majority (LeanDag/Nemo/Basic.lean:48); FinWhale replaces self-parent by leader exclusion (LeanDag/FinWhale/Model/Rule.lean:27–37); Bluestreak requires a quorum only of leader blocks (LeanDag/Bluestreak/Rule.lean:45, 79).

Certified and uncertified DAGs

  • In a certified DAG (Narwhal, Bullshark), each block receives a certificate, built by an extra exchange of signatures, before others may reference it.
  • In an uncertified DAG (Mysticeti and this family), no certificate is sent.
  • A block two rounds above a leader is a certificate for it when its references include n − f blocks that reference the leader.
  • Every direct commit rule is then a threshold on a set of blocks found in the graph.
block→ n − f signatures→ certificate

Illustration: one round of a certified DAG; the block is referenced after its certificate exists.

  • Certifies / CarriesVotes (LeanDag/Mysticeti/Model/Rule.lean:36; LeanDag/Common/Support.lean:324). Threshold shapes: LeanDag/Common/Rules.lean.
  • On the witness: Certifies U3 8 0 (LeanDagTest/Mysticeti/Model.lean:261).

Slots and the leader schedule

  • A slot k has a round and a leader. The schedule may put several leaders in one round and a leader in every round.
  • The candidates of slot k are the blocks of its leader at its round. A correct leader has at most one candidate; a Byzantine leader may have several.
  • Each slot is decided as commit (one candidate) or skip.
  • The ledger is the committed leaders in slot order, each followed by the blocks in its history not yet output.
  • Slots (LeanDag/Common/Slots.lean): slotRound, leader, a kind (default 0, :44), keyed by (round, leader) (:40).
  • Pipelined and two-leader schedules: pipeSlots, duoSlots (LeanDagTest/Mysticeti/Pipelined.lean:53).
  • IsLeaderBlock (LeanDag/Common/Leader.lean:28). A Byzantine leader with two candidates: witness U6 (LeanDagTest/Mysticeti/Model.lean).
  • Ledger: commitSeq, ledgerSet, OutputAt (LeanDag/Common/Ledger.lean).

One decision relation for every rule

A slot is decided in one of four ways:

  1. Direct commit: the rule’s commit condition holds in the validator’s view.
  2. Direct skip: the rule’s skip condition holds.
  3. Indirect commit: a later committed slot (the anchor) links a candidate.
  4. Indirect skip: the anchor links no candidate.

The anchor is the nearest eligible committed slot above; every eligible slot in between must be skipped.

  • AnchoredRule.Decided (LeanDag/Common/Anchored.lean:189). The “in between” premise is hmid.
  • The relation is inductive, not a function. The order of questions in the flowchart is for presentation.

A rule is a card of thresholds

Every rule fills in the same record:

  • the wave: how many rounds above the proposal the direct rules read;
  • the commit and skip conditions;
  • the link from an anchor, possibly in several graded rungs;
  • a tie-break between linked candidates.

Agreement and the agreement of ledgers are proved once, for every rule whose card satisfies a short list of laws.

  • structure AnchoredRule (LeanDag/Common/Anchored.lean:86): waveAt (the direct rules read up to round r + waveAt, as a function of the slot’s kind), Commit, Skip, rungs, Link, tie, Anchor.
  • AnchoredRule.Laws (Anchored.lean:292) is a property of the rule relative to a record invariant. Proved once: decided_agree (:483), decided_mono (:502), commitSeq_agree, ledgerSet_agree, outputAt_agree (:521, 528).
  • Card values: coreAnchored (LeanDag/Mysticeti/Model/Rule.lean:86–95).

Eligibility

  • An anchor at slot j is eligible for slot k when round(k) + wave < round(j).
  • A slot one round above k cannot reach a certificate for k’s leader. A slot two rounds above reaches one only if its own block is a certificate.
  • Anchoring at such slots would let one validator’s direct commit become another validator’s indirect skip.
  • EligibleAt (LeanDag/Common/Anchored.lean:37).
  • ¬ EligibleAt 2 0 1, ¬ EligibleAt 2 0 2, EligibleAt 2 0 3 (LeanDagTest/Mysticeti/Pipelined.lean:72, 77, 80); the commit-to-skip hazard is described at Pipelined.lean:68–72.
  • Reaches is reflexive (LeanDag/Common/CausalHistory.lean:35), which is why a round-r+2 anchor that is itself a certificate does link.
  • Pipelined.lean defines the schedule but no DAG; the figure places pipeSlots leaders (k mod 4) on the Ugrow 6 blocks.

A skip must count blocks

  • The absence of the leader’s block from a view is not a sound reason to skip: a validator cannot distinguish a silent leader from a leader whose block has not yet arrived.
  • In Mysticeti a direct skip needs n − f blocks of the round above that reference no candidate. Those blocks exist, and later blocks do not alter them.
leader block (v1, slot k at round 3k)votecertificate
  • blameSkip q, slotBlamers (LeanDag/Common/Leader.lean:99).
  • ugrow_not_directSkip (LeanDagTest/Mysticeti/Growth.lean:308) covers Ugrow N with N < 3k; the left figure is Ugrow 5, slot 2. ugrow_directCommit (:272) gives the commit in Ugrow 8; ugrow_commits_recur (:332); fairSlots (:260–265).
  • Other rules skip differently (Nemo never skips directly; FinWhale, Hydrozoan, Bluestreak use other counts); their slides say so.

How the results are checked

  • Every definition and theorem is written in Lean 4 and checked by its kernel.
  • A witness is a small concrete DAG, usually 4 to 9 validators, on which Lean computes the verdicts. Witnesses show that hypotheses can be met and that bounds are tight; counterexamples show that a published claim fails.
  • Every DAG in this deck is drawn from a witness. Figures that are not are marked as diagrams.

Mysticeti: direct commit and direct skip

n = 4, f = 1, q = 3. Slot 0 is led by v0; another slot by v3.

  • At round 1, v0, v1, v2 vote for v0's block; v3's block does not.
  • At round 2, the blocks of v0, v1, v2 each reference those three votes: three certificates. 3 ≥ q: commit.
  • At round 1, v0, v1, v2 reference no block of v3 at round 0: three blames. 3 ≥ q: v3's slot is skipped.
U3 (LeanDagTest/Mysticeti/Model.lean:112–127); Certifies U3 8 0 (:261); DirectCommit U3 0 0 (:264); blames U3 3 1 = {0, 1, 2} (:258); DirectSkip U3 3 0 (:267). A direct commit and a direct skip exclude each other: not_directCommit_of_directSkip (LeanDag/Mysticeti/Rule.lean:67).

Mysticeti: indirect commit

  • At round 2 only v0's block is a certificate for L. One certificate is fewer than q, and one blame is fewer than q: no direct decision.
  • The slot at round 3, led by v0, is eligible. It is committed directly by rounds 4 and 5.
  • Its block references v0's certificate, so L is committed indirectly.
U7 (LeanDagTest/Mysticeti/Model.lean:470–495, 526): certificates U7 0 0 = {8}, DirectCommitIn U7 V7 12 3. Why an indirect skip cannot contradict a direct commit: a direct commit puts a certificate in the history of every block from round r + 3, exists_certificate_reaches_of_directCommit (LeanDag/Mysticeti/Rule.lean:79); indirect_agrees_with_direct (:185).

Mysticeti: why it is safe

  1. Two quorums share a correct validator.
  2. A correct validator votes once per round, so a slot has at most one certified candidate.
  3. A direct commit puts a certificate in every history from round r + 3.
  4. A direct skip leaves no certificate anywhere.
  5. So any two views decide every slot the same way, and their ledgers agree.

Nemo-Nemo: the rules on a crash

n = 3, majority 2. Validator 2 creates blocks in rounds 0 and 1, then crashes.

  • Slot 3 (round 3, leader v0): v0 and v1 vote at round 4. 2 ≥ 2: commit.
  • Slot 2 (round 2, leader v2) has no candidate. It has no direct skip; the anchor at slot 4 links nothing for it: indirect skip. Slot 3 is not eligible for slot 2.
Unemo, nemoBlk (LeanDagTest/Nemo/Model.lean:60, 75); nemo_slot0/1/3/4 (:96–109): slots 0, 1, 3, 4 commit directly; slot 3's supporters are {0, 1}. Slot 2 has no candidate (:112); nemo_slot2 (:120), anchor slot 4 (block 11). Ush (LeanDagTest/Nemo/Shadow.lean:32): sh_slot0/2/4 (:49–55); odd_undecided (:74), in every view; sh_not_fairRun (:92). In Ush validator 2 has crashed before round 0 and leads every odd slot.

Odontoceti: direct and indirect

n = 6, f = 1: direct threshold 5, indirect threshold 3. v0 is Byzantine.

  • Slot 0 (leader v0): 5 blames: direct skip.
  • Slot 1: 3 votes, 3 blames: no direct decision. The anchor at slot 3 has voters {1, 2, 3} in its history, 3 ≥ 3: indirect commit.
  • Slot 2: 2 votes, 4 blames: no direct decision. The anchor at slot 4 links nothing: indirect skip.
Uskip (LeanDagTest/Odontoceti/Model.lean): uskip_slot0 (:145–153, blames {1, …, 5}); supporters Uskip 7 2 = {1, 2, 3}, anchor block 21, uskip_slot1 (:157–187); slot 2 supporters {2, 3}, anchor block 28, uskip_slot2 (:202). Round 5 (block 35) supplies slot 4's direct commit. A direct commit is seen with at least n − 3f voters by every block from round r + 2: thickLink_of_directCommit (Odontoceti/Rules.lean:209).

Odontoceti: two twins pass

  • A Byzantine leader can make two blocks (twins) in one round.
  • Both twins can reach the n − 3f threshold inside one anchor's history.
  • If each validator committed any passing twin, two validators could commit different twins.
  • The rule therefore commits the least passing candidate, an order every validator computes the same way.
utwin6_both_pass (LeanDagTest/Odontoceti/Model.lean:250–260). Block 19 is not the slot's committed anchor; at the actual anchor (slot 2, block 15) only twin 0 passes, and utwin6_slot0 commits it (:268–273). x9_both_pass (LeanDagTest/Barnacle/OrcaellaIndirect.lean:249), x9_slot3 (:270), x9_least (:288), under the Hybrid rule orcaella 4 on nine validators. The tie and its law: tie, link_unique in odontocetiLaws (LeanDag/Odontoceti/Decision.lean:161, 173). Counting authors, not blocks: coneSupports (Odontoceti/Rules.lean:75). (informal) That the thesis's argument picks "the" candidate.

Hybrid

  • fb Byzantine validators and fc crash-prone validators. A crash-prone validator never equivocates but may stop.
  • Quorum q = n − fb − fc. The rule is Odontoceti's: q votes to commit, q blames to skip, the least candidate with k voters in the anchor's history to link.
  • k must satisfy 2fb + fc + 1 ≤ k and k + 3fb + 2fc ≤ n. Such a k exists exactly when n ≥ 5fb + 3fc + 1.
  • With fc = 0 the thresholds are Odontoceti's.

Hybrid: the rules on four and five validators

  • fb = 0, fc = 1, n = 4, q = 3: validator 3 stops after round 0. Each slot led by a live validator receives 3 votes: direct commit.
  • fb = 0, fc = 1, n = 5, q = 4, k ∈ {2, 3}: slot 1 receives 2 votes and 3 blames, so no direct decision. Both voters are in the history of the anchor at slot 3. At k = 2 slot 1 is committed; at k = 3 it is skipped.
Uhyb4 (LeanDagTest/Hybrid/Model.lean:36–83), uhyb4_slot1 (:98). The crashed validator's slot is not directly skipped (uhyb4_slot3_not_directSkip, :116). U5 (LeanDagTest/Barnacle/OrcaellaIndirect.lean): u5_commit (:129), u5_skip (:143). In U5 nobody crashes; the split is produced by the references alone.

Hybrid: the committee bound is tight

With fb = 1, fc = 1 and n = 8 (one fewer than 5fb + 3fc + 1 = 9), no k is admissible. For every k, one full view of one DAG derives both a commit and a skip for the same slot.

FinWhale

  • Committee n = 3f + 2p − 1, with 1 ≤ p ≤ f. Safety: up to f Byzantine. Fast path: when at most p are Byzantine.
  • Three thresholds: slow 2f + p, block validity n − f, fast n − p.
  • Fast commit at round r + 1: n − p votes.
  • Slow commit at round r + 2: 2f + p blocks, each referencing 2f + p votes.
  • Validity: if two of a block's references reference two different blocks of v, the block may not reference a block of v (leader exclusion).
  • p = 1 gives n = 3f + 1; p = f gives n = 5f − 1.

Compared with Mysticeti: a second, faster commit rule at r + 1; the skip and the indirect rule also read "evidence" (slide 29); a different committee; leader exclusion instead of self-parent.
The parameter p sets both the committee size and the number of faults the fast path tolerates.
The committee grows with p. Beyond p faults only the slow path commits. There is no self-parent rule, so inclusion of every block is not proved.

FinWhale: fast and slow commit

f = 2, p = 2, n = 9; validators 0 and 1 are Byzantine.

  • Fast. Seven round-1 blocks reference the leader's block: 7 ≥ 7, commit at round 1.
  • Slow. Every round-2 block references 7 votes; six such blocks suffice: 6 ≥ 6 certificates, commit at round 2.
leader blockvotecertificateshaded: six certificates counted

Witness Dfast, LeanDagTest/FinWhale/Model.lean

Dfast (LeanDagTest/FinWhale/Model.lean:88): voters = {0, …, 6}, FastCommit Dfast 0 (:103, 105); every round-2 block has 7 voting parents (:115) and is an SP-certificate (:117); SPCommit from 6 certificates (:120). Latency: fastCommit_latency (LeanDag/FinWhale/Reactive.lean:98): after GST, with a correct leader and at most p Byzantine, every correct round-1 block is built within Δ + δ + 2·proc of its author entering round 0; no_timeout_of_fast (:118). (informal) "Two message delays" is a reading of this bound.

FinWhale: skip and evidence

  • A round-r+2 block is evidence for l when it references at least f + p − 1 votes for l; if its references show the leader equivocating, at least f + p for l and at most f + p − 1 for every other candidate.
  • Direct skip: 2f + p blocks at r + 1 reference no candidate, and 2f + p blocks at r + 2 are evidence for nothing.
  • Indirect commit: the anchor's history holds a slow certificate for l, or 2f + p evidence blocks for l. The least such l is committed.
  • Evidence is needed because a fast commit may leave no slow certificate.
FPEvidence (LeanDag/FinWhale/Model/Rule.lean:135), branching on ExposesEquivocationBy (:122). DirectSkip (LeanDag/FinWhale/Model/Decision.lean:67); SPSkip (LeanDag/FinWhale/Model/Skip.lean:42); NonFPEvidence (Skip.lean:32). FinWhale: what the formalisation found

  • The paper's counting argument for Lemma 22 covers only p = 1. For p ≥ 2 (smallest case n = 9) the lemma is proved by a pigeonhole argument.
  • In the paper's case C3 of Lemmas 18 and 19 the count has no margin at p = 1; the lemmas are proved instead by induction on the time a block is built.
  • The paper's proofs of Lemmas 6 and 7 pass through the slow skip, which does not apply when a validator holds no block of the slot; they are proved through the evidence quorum.
  • The paper's latency claim (Definition 1) is proved, and the evidence count is exactly tight at n = 3f + 2p − 1 and one short at n − 1.
window_margin (LeanDag/FinWhale/Counting.lean:143): the cyclic window works iff p ≤ 1. lemma22 (LeanDag/FinWhale/Rotation.lean:187) holds for all p, through three_correct_window (:143). c3_margin (Counting.lean:156), c3_reachable (:149); lemma18, lemma19 (LeanDag/FinWhale/Creation.lean:76, 128). no_directSkip_of_commit_view (LeanDag/FinWhale/View.lean:216), no_indirectCommit_of_directSkip_view (:265); witness Vmiss (LeanDagTest/FinWhale/Equivocation.lean:247–270). fastCommit_latency (Reactive.lean:98). equivocating_margin (Counting.lean:130) is arithmetic tightness of the count, not a lower bound for every protocol. (informal) Which of these the paper states without proof.

Hydrozoan

  • f Byzantine, c crashed, a slack k ≥ 0: n ≥ 3f + 2c + k + 1.
  • Thresholds: p = ⌊(c + k)/2⌋, q = n − f − c, qFast = n − p, qCert = ⌊(n + f)/2⌋ + 1, qSlow = 2f + c + 1, qWeak = f + p + 1.
  • Fast commit: qFast votes at r + 1. Slow commit: qSlow certificates at r + 2, each referencing qCert votes.
  • Skip: qFast blames at r + 1.
  • Indirect, two rungs: (1) a certificate in the anchor’s history; (2) if no candidate has one, the least candidate with qWeak votes in the anchor’s history.
  • Faults.card_replicas (LeanDag/Hydrozoan/Model/Faults.lean:41); thresholds (:53–74). FastCommit (LeanDag/Hydrozoan/Model/DirectRules.lean:45); SlowCommit, IsCertificate, certificates (:40, 50, 62); SkippedLeader (:73). hydrozoanAnchored (LeanDag/Hydrozoan/Model/Decided.lean:28–42). Rung-0-empty premise: Decided.indirectCommit (LeanDag/Common/Anchored.lean:201).
  • Values at n = 7: LeanDagTest/Hydrozoan/Model.lean:42–45.
  • FastLatency (LeanDag/Hydrozoan/DirectLiveness/Proof.lean:28) is outside the liveness statement; CommitLiveness (LeanDag/Hydrozoan/DirectLiveness/Statement.lean:29) is the guarantee.

Hydrozoan: why the second rung exists

n = 7; v0 is Byzantine and equivocates; v1 has crashed.

  • The leader receives exactly qFast = 6 votes: fast commit.
  • No block is a certificate: each round-2 block references only 4 votes, one fewer than qCert = 5.
  • A validator that missed the fast commit consults the anchor. Rung 1 finds no certificate. Rung 2 finds 4 voters, at least qWeak = 3: commit.
  • U4, V4 (lk4, 32 blocks; LeanDagTest/Hydrozoan/DirectSafety.lean): FastCommit U4 2 0, certificates U4 2 0 = ∅, supporters U4 2 1 = {0, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6}; the anchor reaches 4 voters (checked by evaluation; the witness’s docstring states the same). V4 withholds voter 13, so every direct rule fails in view.
  • WeakLinked (LeanDag/Hydrozoan/Model/IndirectRules.lean).

Hydrozoan: what the formalisation found

  • The six threshold inequalities hold for every slack k ≥ 0.
  • One of them must be strengthened to qFast + q − n − f ≥ qWeak, so that every eligible anchor sees at least qWeak votes of every fast commit.
  • Round-robin by slot is not fair inside the bound: at n = 5, f = 0, c = 2, it need not place three live leaders consecutively. A rotation aligned to waves is fair.
  • ThresholdArithmetic.Statement / holds (LeanDag/Hydrozoan/ThresholdArithmetic/Statement.lean:61, Proof.lean:13). Row 6 of the statement is the weaker AnchorSeesFast (Statement.lean:56); the strengthened form is n_add_qWeak_add_f_le_qFast_add_q (LeanDag/Hydrozoan/Helpers/SlotAgreement.lean:52).
  • (informal) The paper’s cap k ≤ 2f + c − 4 appears only in a docstring (LeanDagTest/OptimalHydrozoan/Thresholds.lean:232).
  • fiveCrashy, ¬ FairRunOn (S := slotRobin) Correct 3 (LeanDagTest/Hydrozoan/Grounding.lean:135, 160); WaveRobinFair (LeanDag/Hydrozoan/Grounding/Statement.lean).
  • Properties: Agree, CommitsCandidate, SkipsUnsupported (LeanDag/Hydrozoan/Properties/Statement.lean:27, Proof.lean:35), commitsDirect (Helpers/Commit.lean:298), quorate (Helpers/Carrier.lean:47); safety, progress (Properties/Proof.lean:44–49).

Optimal-Hydrozoan

  • Hydrozoan’s committee, with at least one tolerated fault (f + c ≥ 1).
  • The fast path tolerates one more fault: pOpt = p + 1, qFastOpt = n − pOpt.
  • FinWhale’s evidence: a round-r+2 block is evidence for L when it references tPlain = n − (2f + c + pOpt) votes for L; or, if it saw the leader equivocate, tEquiv = f + pOpt votes with every rival below tEquiv.
  • Skip: qCert blames and qCert round-r+2 blocks that are evidence for nothing.
  • Indirect: (1) a certificate; (2) qCert evidence blocks in the anchor’s history. No tie-break.
  • OptimalFaults (LeanDag/OptimalHydrozoan/Model/Faults.lean:23–27); pOpt (:36), qFastOpt (:42), tPlain (:49), tEquiv (:55).
  • IsFastEvidence (LeanDag/OptimalHydrozoan/Model/DirectRules.lean:55); SkippedLeaderOpt (:88, decision round :83–90); optimalAnchored (Model/Decided.lean:29–41, tie = False); EvidenceLinked (Model/IndirectRules.lean:24).

Optimal-Hydrozoan: the evidence rung

n = 4. The leader equivocates (copies 4 and 5).

  • Copy 4 receives 3 votes: fast commit. No block is a certificate.
  • Each round-r+2 block sees both copies, references 2 votes for copy 4 and 1 for copy 5, and is evidence for copy 4.
  • The anchor’s history holds the three evidence blocks: rung 2 commits copy 4.
  • OE (lkE; LeanDagTest/OptimalHydrozoan/SlotAgreement.lean:127, 162): supporters UE 4 2 = {0, 1, 3}, certificates UE 4 1 = ∅ (:175), EvidenceLinked UE 18 4 1 (:181), oe_slot1_evidence (:186).
  • Block 11 votes for copy 5. The leader’s slot is at round r = 1; the evidence blocks are at round 3.

Bluestreak

  • n ≥ 3f + 1, quorum n − f.
  • Sparse DAG: only leader blocks must reference n − f blocks. Other blocks reference their own previous block and, optionally, leader blocks.
  • A round-r+2 block claims L by naming it in its payload, or by referencing n − f votes for it.
  • Direct commit: n − f claims for a leader-tagged L.
  • Direct skip: n − f round-r+1 blocks in view, and for each candidate n − f of them that omit it.
  • Indirect: a claim for a tagged L in the anchor’s history.
Compared with Mysticeti: most blocks reference two blocks instead of n − f; a certificate is replaced by a claim, which only names the block.
Far fewer references per block. Three rounds at n = 3f + 1.
Blocks need not reference a quorum, so chain-quality coverage is not shown. Claims require a discipline (slide 39).
  • roleClause (LeanDag/Bluestreak/Rule.lean:45); ValidWrt with self-parent (:79). (informal) “At most two references” is a docstring (:77–78).
  • Claims (:124), claimers (:131); Commit = DirectCommitIn ∧ Tagged (:138, 189); DirectSkipIn (:144); Link = ClaimedIn ∧ Tagged, one rung, no tie (:192–194).
  • Quorate is not shown for Bluestreak (LeanDag/Bluestreak/Carrier.lean:19–21).
  • Figures: U3 (LeanDagTest/Mysticeti/Model.lean) has rounds 0–2 only; Bluestreak U1 (LeanDagTest/Bluestreak/Model.lean:73) is drawn at rounds 0–3.

Bluestreak: direct and indirect

n = 4, leader of slot k is v(k mod 4).

  • Slot 0 has 3 votes but only 2 claims (blocks 8 and 10): not decided directly.
  • Slots 1–3 are committed directly.
  • The anchor, block 15, references block 8, which claims block 0: slot 0 is committed indirectly.
  • U1 (LeanDagTest/Bluestreak/Model.lean:73): Certified U1 0 (:84), claimers U1 0 = {8, 10} (:85), no direct decision (:87), U1_slot1/2/3 (:91–95), U1_slot0 (:100).
  • Block 8 claims 0 in its payload; leader block 10 claims 0 by referencing its 3 votes 4, 5, 7.

Bluestreak: an anchor must be committed

  • A claim names a block; the votes behind it need not be in the claimer’s history.
  • A Byzantine block can claim a slot that a quorum skipped.
  • So the indirect rule is safe only at a committed anchor: every committed anchor is certified, backed and leader-tagged. Of the rules here, only Bluestreak requires this field.
  • skip_link (LeanDag/Common/Anchored.lean:324) has the premise R.Anchor U A; bluestreakLaws (LeanDag/Bluestreak/Safety.lean:183); Anchor = Certified ∧ Backed ∧ Tagged (LeanDag/Bluestreak/Rule.lean:195), proved of committed anchors by anchor_commit, anchor_link (Safety.lean:193–199). Default Anchor = True (Anchored.lean:118).
  • U2: DirectSkipIn (LeanDagTest/Bluestreak/Model.lean:164), ClaimedIn U2 15 0 (:167), ¬ Certified U2 15 (:168). U2 has no committed block. Validator 3 is Byzantine (bsFaults2); block 0 has one vote (block 4).

Bluestreak: the claim discipline

  • From round 2, a correct block’s claim must name a block certified exactly two rounds below.
  • Safety, liveness and every mechanism assume this discipline.
  • Read two rounds deep, the discipline is preserved by garbage collection.
  • BackedClaim (LeanDag/Bluestreak/Rule.lean:153), Disciplined (:175); bluestreakLaws under Invariant := Disciplined (LeanDag/Bluestreak/Safety.lean:162–167); carrier is the Disciplined subtype (Carrier.lean:35); ReactiveB.disciplined (LeanDag/Bluestreak/Reactive.lean:126); disciplined_chop (LeanDag/Bluestreak/Record.lean:50).
  • (informal) That the paper’s unbounded reading would make garbage collection impossible.

Mahi-Mahi

  • n ≥ 3f + 1. A wave of w rounds: propose at r, vote at r + w − 2, certify at r + w − 1. At w = 3 this is Mysticeti.
  • A block votes for the least block of the leader’s round found in its history (not only among its direct references).
  • A direct skip blames the slot: the blamer has no block of the slot in its history.
  • The leader of a wave is revealed only after the wave, so the adversary cannot direct its message scheduling against it.
Compared with Mysticeti: a longer wave, votes found anywhere in the history, a skip per slot, and an unpredictable leader.
Live with no timing assumption about the network.
More rounds per commit; it needs an unpredictable leader (a common coin).
  • votingRound (LeanDag/MahiMahi/Model/Rules.lean:34), decisionRoundAt (:40), Votes (:55), Blames (:63), DirectSkip (:110).
  • w = 3 equals Mysticeti: DecidedConservative (LeanDag/Steelhead/MahiMahiPair/Safety/Statement.lean:152).
  • Safety for w ≥ 2 (MahiMahiProperties.safety, LeanDag/MahiMahi/Properties.lean:407); liveness for w ≥ 4 (:315, 392).
  • Liveness hypothesis UnpredictableWithin (LeanDag/MahiMahi/Model/Unpredictable.lean:38). (informal) The coin itself is modelled only in the Steelhead arc.

Mahi-Mahi: votes and what a wave commits

  • At w ≥ 4 a history can contain two twins of the leader; a block votes only for the least.
  • At w ≥ 4, once a correct quorum produces through the wave, some correct validator’s block is directly committed.
  • At w ≥ 5, at least n − f − b correct validators are good: their block would commit if chosen (b = number of Byzantine).
  • An adversary that knows the leader in advance can prevent the leader’s block from entering the other validators’ histories.
  • twin4: twins 0 and 4 lie in block 8’s history; 8 votes for 0.
  • aim4: block 5 enters no other history up to round 3. Good at w = 4: {0, 2, 3} (shaded); at w = 5: all.
leader blockvoteblame

  • GoodNonempty (LeanDag/MahiMahi/Counting/Statement.lean:47); GoodCard (:67, 81): n − f ≤ |goodAt ∩ Correct| + |byzantine|; goodAt (LeanDag/MahiMahi/Model/Good.lean:29).
  • goodAt aim4 4 1 = {0, 2, 3} (LeanDagTest/MahiMahi/Counting.lean:84); goodAt aim4 5 1 = univ (:102); ¬ UnpredictableWithin aim4 4 1 5 with a fair schedule (LeanDagTest/MahiMahi/Liveness.lean:71, 82).
  • In aim4 slot 1 (block 5) is directly skipped at w = 4: only block 13 votes, blocks 12, 14, 15 blame; at w = 5 it is committed.

Mahi-Mahi: what the formalisation found

  • The paper counts all n − f validators in the common core as good. Twins of Byzantine leaders can split the votes, so the proved count is n − f − b.
  • Proved commit probability per wave, at w ≥ 5: at least (n − f − b)/n, which is always at least 1/3. At n = 4, f = b = 1: 1/2.
  • 2f + 1 leader slots per round guarantee a commit at w ≥ 5.
  • Mysticeti skips per candidate; Mahi-Mahi skips per slot.
  • GoodCard as above. CommitProbability (LeanDag/Steelhead/MahiMahiPair/Coin/Statement.lean:193): (n − f − b)/n ≤ commitProb and 1/3 ≤ commitProb at wa ≥ 5; at w = 4 only 1/n (CommitProbabilityFour, :205).
  • MultiLeader (LeanDag/MahiMahi/Counting/Statement.lean:88) proves 2f + 1 suffice. (informal) The paper’s f + 1 and 2/3.
  • DirectSkip (Rules.lean:106–112); mahiMahiAnchored (LeanDag/MahiMahi/Model/Decision.lean:60).

Async BlueBottle

  • n ≥ 5f + 1. Propose at r; vote and decide at r + 2, with votes found in the history as in Mahi-Mahi; no certificates.
  • Direct commit: n − f votes. Direct skip: n − f blames.
  • Indirect: n − 3f voters in the anchor’s history; the least passing candidate is committed.
  • The leader is unpredictable, as in Mahi-Mahi.
Compared with Odontoceti: the vote round moves from r + 1 to r + 2 and votes are found anywhere in the history, so that the rule is live with an unpredictable leader.
Live with no timing assumption, three rounds per wave; commit probability at least (n − 3f)/n per wave.
Six validators per fault and an unpredictable leader.

  • SkipsUnsupported is not established for this rule.

Async BlueBottle: witnesses

  • n = 6: the leader’s block enters no history but its own. Five blames: direct skip. The schedule is fair, but the leader was known in advance.
  • Two twins can both pass the n − 3f test at one anchor: the least must be chosen.
  • The paper’s procedure skips per candidate, which can skip one twin while the other is committed.

Steelhead

  • Each slot has a kind: synchronous (a known leader, short wave ws) or asynchronous (an unpredictable leader, long wave wa).
  • A slot is decided by the rule of its kind, at its own wave; its anchor lies at or above round + w(kind).
  • A period P sets the kinds: round r is asynchronous when r mod P = 0. The period is adapted at intervals of I rounds.
  • Two instances: Mysticeti with Mahi-Mahi (n ≥ 3f + 1, waves 3 and wa ≥ 4), and Odontoceti with Async BlueBottle (n ≥ 5f + 1, waves 2 and 3).
Compared with Mysticeti: two rules on one DAG, chosen per slot, and a controller that chooses how often the asynchronous rule runs.
Short waves while the network is synchronous; liveness under asynchrony.
Two rules, a coin, a period controller, and a failover (slide 47).
  • wavelength (LeanDag/Steelhead/Model/Wavelength.lean:40); periodicKind, IsAsync (:48, 59); steelheadAnchored (LeanDag/Steelhead/Model/Decision.lean:48–54, waveAt = w κ − 1); compose (LeanDag/Steelhead/Model/Compose.lean:31); mahiMahiPair, blueBottlePair (LeanDag/Steelhead/Model/Pair.lean:43, 52); pair_tie (least, for the 5f + 1 pair; LeanDag/Steelhead/Helpers/BlueBottlePair.lean).
  • PeriodAt (LeanDag/Steelhead/Model/Period.lean); anchorUpdate (LeanDag/Steelhead/Model/Replay.lean:310) is one update rule; any is allowed.
  • Reading the anchor floor at ws for every slot is unsafe: lowFloor (LeanDagTest/Steelhead/Model.lean:170, 188, 194).

Steelhead: the stall

  • At any period P ≥ ws, an adversary delivers each synchronous leader’s block to exactly f + 1 validators. Neither a commit nor a skip quorum forms.
  • The synchronous slot just below each asynchronous round is then undecided in every view, and the output does not advance beyond it.
  • A committed asynchronous slot does not decide the synchronous slots below it.
  • At period 1 every slot is proved to be decided.
  • Stall (LeanDag/Steelhead/MahiMahiPair/Liveness/Statement.lean:611): slots at rounds ≡ P − 1 (mod P) are never decided, under “no synchronous certificate and no synchronous direct skip”. AllDecidedBelowAtPeriodOne (:639). Nothing is stated for period 2.
  • st20 (LeanDagTest/Steelhead/Counterexamples/Stall.lean:70, 101–117, st20_slot0 :129, st20_stall_view :170): candidates 6, 11, 12 have voters {9, 10}, {14, 15}, {16, 17}; round 4 certifies block 1. Validator 0 is Byzantine.
  • rt_stall (LeanDagTest/Steelhead/Counterexamples/RotatingStall.lean:270).

Steelhead: control and failover

  • The period is changed by a second verdict, read at the asynchronous control slots of each interval.
  • Failover: when the anchor is more than I rounds above the last committed output, the next interval runs at period 1.
  • Under failover a stalled slot is decided almost surely. The probability it is still undecided after M blocks, each of wa·K coins, is at most 2 · ((nwa·K − (n − f − b)wa·K) / nwa·K)⌊M/2⌋, where b is the number of Byzantine validators and K bounds the period.
  • ControlDecided, controlRound, controlSlots (LeanDag/Steelhead/Model/Chain.lean:79–129); PeriodAt.anchor (Model/Period.lean:144); PeriodOne (LeanDag/Steelhead/MahiMahiPair/Period/Statement.lean:277).
  • UndecidedTail (LeanDag/Steelhead/MahiMahiPair/Coin/Statement.lean:277), badBlockBound (:265); K is the period bound; hypotheses 5 ≤ wa, K ≤ I, wa ≤ I, wa·K ≤ q·I; DecidedAlmostSurely (:461).
  • rt_failover, rt_recovers (LeanDagTest/Steelhead/Failover.lean:345, 384); rtPer: periods 4, 4, 1, 1; the coin names validator 2 at every round; anchors rt_anchor0/1/2 at rounds 4, 12, 17 (:196, 211, 225).

Steelhead: what the formalisation found

  • The paper’s period update alone retains a stalled period; liveness requires the failover.
  • An equivocating leader at a slot’s anchor floor can hold the slot undecided.
  • The interval must satisfy I ≥ 2·maxPeriod and I ≥ maxPeriod + wa − 2.
  • In the paper’s timeout appendix, with exactly one vote missing, a certificate forms with probability f/n, not (n − f)/n.
  • anchorUpdate_half_retains (LeanDag/Steelhead/Helpers/Replay.lean:821); rt_update_four, rt_no_output_above_two (RotatingStall.lean:287, 302).
  • bf30_slot0_undecided (LeanDagTest/Steelhead/Counterexamples/ByzantineFloor.lean:184).
  • TwoAsyncRounds, TwoAsyncRoundsInWindow (Period/Statement.lean:295, 379); WindowResolves (:336); rw44_keeps_two (LeanDagTest/Steelhead/Counterexamples/ReplayShortWindow.lean:98).
  • CertProbEdges (LeanDag/Steelhead/MahiMahiPair/Timeout/Statement.lean:43).
  • (informal) How many findings the paper adopted.

Minnow: the rule

  • n ≥ 3f + 1; no self-parent rule.
  • Commit a leader block l when n − f processes reference it from the round above, and every earlier leader slot is resolved: one of its blocks is in l's history, or is concurrent with l and committed or skipped.
  • Skip when n − f processes of the round above have no block that references it.
  • The rule consults no later anchor.

A commit needs a quorum in the round above and every earlier slot resolved; the rule reads no later anchor.

Minnow.ValidHere (LeanDag/Minnow/Model/Rule.lean:43); Quorum (:119); Skipped (:134; the vertex-counting reading SkippedByVertex, :145, lets one vertex be committed and skipped, LeanDagTest/Minnow/Skip.lean:60, 69); CommittedAt (:161).

Minnow: an earlier leader committed after a later one

n = 4. Process 0 equivocates at round 0: blocks 0 and 4. Block 4 is referenced by process 1 only.

  • A validator missing block 5 sees the round-1 leader block 6 reach block 4, which resolves slot 0. Block 6 is committed, while slot 0 is still undecided.
  • Block 5 arrives. Block 0 now has a quorum and is committed for slot 0, after the later leader.

Initial state: the twins 0 and 4 and their references. Step 1: the partial view commits block 6. Step 2: the full view commits block 0 for the earlier slot.

LeanDagTest/Minnow/Safety.lean: slotBlocks Dfull (0,0) = {0, 4} (:86, 91); Reaches Dpart 6 4, CommittedAt Dpart sfLead 1 6 (:112, 116); Dfull adds blocks 5 and 12 (:96, 126); block 4 is never committed (¬ Quorum Dfull 4, :179); the violated property is Safe-Commit (:134).

Minnow: slots that are never decided

The Byzantine process's blocks reach two processes of four: too few to commit, too many to skip. A slot that is resolved only by a block in a leader's history holds later leaders for two rounds.

LeanDagTest/Minnow/Deadlock.lean: 2 of 4 pointers (:86, 89); mLead (:79, 109–146); Ds (:205–223). LeanDagTest/Minnow/Fair.lean: CommittedAt Dm mFair 2 11 (:92). not_committedAt_of_dead (LeanDag/Minnow/Blocking.lean:40). (informal) That 2f + 1 is the least safe skip threshold, so the gap cannot be closed.

Black Marlin: the rule

  • n ≥ 3f + 1; one anchor per round; no certificates.
  • Commit an anchor B at round r when n − f validators reference it at round r + 1, and some anchor at r + 1 references B and is itself referenced by n − f validators at r + 2.
  • There is no skip. Anchors that are not committed are output through a descent from a later committed anchor.

Rotation.anchor, IsAnchor, Supported, Linked, Committed (LeanDag/BlackMarlin/Model/Rules.lean:37, 51, 63, 83, 94); descend, flushRecord (LeanDag/BlackMarlin/Model/Descent.lean:85, 100). Black Marlin has no carrier. (informal) "No reliable broadcast, no coin".

Black Marlin: agreement fails

n = 4, f = 1. Validator 0 equivocates at round 2: blocks 8 and 12.

  • Block 8 is committed; block 12 is not supported.
  • The committed anchor 19 at round 4 omits block 14.
  • One validator outputs block 8 for round 2; another outputs block 12.

Total order also fails, on blocks 5 and 7 of correct validators.

Initial state: the twins 8 and 12. Step 1: 8 is supported by 14, 15, 16 and linked through anchor 14; 12 has one supporter. Step 2: the validator that missed round 2 commits 19, whose descent takes 12.

LeanDagTest/BlackMarlin/Divergence.lean: divBlk (:71), twins (:57, 115), commit of 8 and non-support of 12 (:120), anchor 19 omits 14 (:124), Committed Udiv 19 4 (:129), differing outputs (:135, 154, 182); total order (:261, 298). Sound lemmas: eq_of_supported, reaches_of_supported, reaches_of_committed_of_le, quorum_authorsAt_of_lt (LeanDag/BlackMarlin/Helpers/Rules.lean:40, 59, 77, 110).

Every rule on one page

Rounds to commit = waveAt + 1; for Minnow and Black Marlin, the rounds their commit rules read (Quorum, LeanDag/Minnow/Model/Rule.lean:119; Committed, LeanDag/BlackMarlin/Model/Rules.lean:94). Sources: the rule records cited on each protocol's slide; FinWhale LeanDag/FinWhale/Model/Decided.lean:24; Hybrid's committee through Admissible (HybridFaults itself asks 3(fb + fc) + 1, LeanDag/Hybrid/Faults.lean:38).

What the formalisation found, by rule

Each row is detailed, with its Lean evidence, on the rule's slides.

Three recurring lessons

  1. Fix an order. Wherever two twins can pass a test, the choice between them must be made by an order every validator computes.
  2. Count, do not infer from absence. A skip must count blocks that exist.
  3. Use later evidence. Every rule proved safe here has an indirect rule that reads a later committed anchor; the two refuted rules have none.
  • 1: tie = (<) in Odontoceti, Hybrid, FinWhale, Hydrozoan (second rung), Async BlueBottle; Mahi-Mahi's Votes picks the least block.
  • 2: ugrow_not_directSkip (LeanDagTest/Mysticeti/Growth.lean:308).
  • 3: every carrier has rungs ≥ 1; Black Marlin and Minnow have no anchor rule. (informal) That the missing rule causes the failures.
Part III

Properties

From rules to properties

Mechanisms such as garbage collection or crash recovery should not be proved once per rule. Instead:

  • each rule is proved to have a few properties;
  • each mechanism is proved once, using only those properties.

Eleven rules (all but Minnow and Black Marlin) have the properties.

The diagram of slide 2, with the properties highlighted. The eleven carriers are listed in the notes of slide 2.

The carrier

A mechanism accesses a rule only through its carrier:

  • a type of universes (all blocks) and of views (what one validator holds);
  • the round, creator and references of each block;
  • the decision relation: under schedule S, view V decides slot k as v.

Laws: a view holds only universe blocks; a view holds every block that its blocks reference; references go one round down.

DagRule (LeanDag/Properties/Carrier.lean:31); Decided is a relation Slots → View U → ℕ → Option BlockId → Prop (:56); viewSound (:45), viewComplete (:49), causal (:54). Eleven carriers (slide 2).

Banded: a verdict reads a finite band of rounds

Each verdict depends only on the blocks in a band of rounds, from the slot's round to some round top. Any other universe, view and schedule that match in the band — up to a shift of round and slot numbers — reach the same verdict.

leader blockvotecertificate

The band of the slot of block 11 is rounds 3–5 of Uexcl and rounds 1–3 of the cut; the verdict is the same in both.

Banded (LeanDag/Properties/Band.lean:227): the other view holds at least the original view's blocks inside the band; slot rounds, leaders and kinds match there. Used by LocalTruncate.of_banded (LeanDag/Properties/Derived/Truncate.lean:38), Persist.of_banded (LeanDag/Properties/Derived/FromBand.lean:25), Stack.safe_and_live (LeanDag/Properties/Arcs/Stack.lean:109), safety (LeanDag/Properties/Arcs/Headline.lean:63). Witness: DirectCommit Uexcl 11 3, DirectCommit (chop Uexcl 2) 11 1 (LeanDagTest/GC/Chop.lean:60–61); slot 1 of Uexcl is slot 0 of the chopped schedule (:72–84).

Agree, CommitsCandidate, Indirect

  • Agree: two views of one universe never decide a slot differently, skips included.
  • CommitsCandidate: a committed block is a candidate of its slot.
  • Indirect: a committed eligible anchor, with every eligible slot in between skipped, decides the slot; changing the other slots' leaders does not change that verdict.

Agree (LeanDag/Properties/Agree.lean:22); CommitsCandidate (LeanDag/Properties/Candidate.lean:50); Indirect (LeanDag/Properties/Commit.lean:40). Indirect gives Descends (Descends.of_indirect, LeanDag/Properties/Derived/Descent.lean:83).

The support: the conditions for a commit

  • A support names the wave and what it means for a block to certify a candidate.
  • Law 1 (local): certification depends only on the wave's rounds, so it is unchanged by cutting or shifting rounds outside them.
  • Law 2 (commits): if a reliable quorum T leads a slot, produces through its wave and certifies every candidate, then a view that holds those rounds commits the slot.
  • Liveness needs exactly this, at every slot T leads. The network assumption is used only to establish it.

Support (LeanDag/Properties/Support.lean:39), Local (:92), Commits (:103). Support.live (LeanDag/Properties/Derived/LeaderCommits.lean:40): production and certification at the T-led slots of a window. live_of_coverage (LeanDag/Timed/Coverage.lean:108); coreSupport_live_of_reactiveLive (LeanDag/Reactive/MysticetiProperties.lean:59). No synchrony name appears under LeanDag/Properties/ (checked by scripts/check-arc-holes.py, a Makefile step).

Optional and derived properties

Optional, needed by one mechanism each:

  • CommitsDirect: a direct commit is a verdict (adaptive leader count).
  • SkipsUnsupported: a slot is skipped when a large enough set, present one round above, references none of its candidates (prompt skip).
  • Quorate: every block references n − f distinct creators (chain quality).
  • SelfParent, NoEquiv: every block references its creator's previous block; a reliable creator makes one block per round (inclusion).
  • CommitsDirect (LeanDag/Properties/Optional/Direct.lean:25), used by LeanDag/Barnacle/Healthy/Statement.lean:101. SkipsUnsupported (Optional/Skip.lean:51). Quorate (Optional/Quorate.lean:33), for non-genesis blocks, n − slack with slack = f in the core reliability. SelfParent, NoEquiv (Optional/SelfParent.lean:23, 28).
  • Derivations: Persist.of_banded, LocalTruncate.of_banded, Support.leaderCommits (Derived/LeaderCommits.lean:50), Descends.of_indirect.
  • Some rules also prove them directly: Mysticeti proves LeaderCommits (leaderCommits_cert, LeanDag/Mysticeti/Properties.lean:534) and derives Law 2 from it (:634); Steelhead's persist (LeanDag/Steelhead/Properties.lean:158).

Safety, for every rule and every mechanism

From Banded, Agree and CommitsCandidate, across any sequence of cuts, recoveries and re-geneses:

  • every verdict above the settling round is the same before and after;
  • any view after agrees with any view before, above the settling round;
  • every commit is a candidate, and no block is committed at two slots;
  • adding blocks never changes a verdict.

Safe (LeanDag/Properties/Arcs/Headline.lean:46), safety (:63), Safe.prefix_agree (:76). The last bullet is the conjunct on Extends.

Liveness, for every rule

From Law 2, CommitsCandidate, SelfParent and NoEquiv:

  • Progress: every slot below a run of reliably led slots is decided, and reliably led slots continue to be committed.
  • Inclusion: every block of a reliable validator enters the ledger, through a later slot its creator leads.

Seven rules have both. Nemo, FinWhale, Hydrozoan and Optimal-Hydrozoan lack SelfParent and have progress only.

Progresses (Headline.lean:94), Includes (:105), Lives (:117), liveness (:139); Progresses takes Descends as a hypothesis. Progress only: LeanDag/Nemo/Properties.lean:242, LeanDag/FinWhale/Carrier.lean:360, LeanDag/Hydrozoan/Properties/Proof.lean:47, LeanDag/OptimalHydrozoan/Carrier.lean:290.

The properties a user sees

Part IV

Mechanisms

The mechanisms

Each row is detailed, with its Lean evidence, on the slides listed. The storage bound is stated over the delivery model (LeanDag/DoS/) and reads no property of the rule.

Liveness, and the role of time

  • The commit rule counts references; it does not refer to time.
  • Liveness is reduced to two facts about the DAG, from some round on:
    • every reliable validator has a block in each round;
    • each reliable block references every reliable block of the round below.
  • These follow from view convergence and the pacemaker's rules.
Uses: view convergence and the pacemaker's rules (slide 69).
Gives: the support's precondition live (slide 61).

The two facts are PopulatedOn (LeanDag/Common/Participation.lean:62) and SynchronisedOn (:80). The pacemaker is PaceCore (LeanDag/Mysticeti/ViewPace.lean:114).

Mysticeti's route: certifiesAt_of_synchronisedOn (LeanDag/Mysticeti/Liveness.lean:95) gives a direct commit; Support.live (LeanDag/Properties/Derived/LeaderCommits.lean:40).

The pacemaker's rules

  • Advance: a validator holding blocks of n − f creators at round n moves past round n.
  • Catch up: after GST, a validator that holds a reliable block of round n enters round n within proc, the time to process and build a block.
  • Wait: a validator spends at least timeout(n) in round n.
  • Reference: a validator's block references every block of the previous round that it holds.

PaceCore.advances (LeanDag/Mysticeti/ViewPace.lean:171), catchup (:182), ViewPace.waits (:349: built v n + timeout n ≤ built v (n+1)), references (:351).

Drift collapses in one round

  • Validators' clocks may drift apart before GST.
  • After GST, catching up brings every reliable validator within Δ + proc of the others in one round, whatever the spread before.
  • A timeout of 2Δ + proc therefore suffices; it does not depend on the spread before GST.

PaceCore.drift_collapse (ViewPace.lean:289), driftOn_of_catchup (:306, 428); synchronisedOn_of_converges (:461), directCommit_of_wait (:708), decided_of_wait (:721), each with 2·delay + proc ≤ timeout n.

Witness ugrowLag (LeanDagTest/Reactive/Collapse.lean:65: gst = 12, delay = 2, proc = 1, timeout = 5); ugrowLag_collapse (:208), ugrowLag_decided (:230, no spread hypothesis). v0 and v1 enter every round at the same time, so their lines coincide.

(informal) "Waiting alone does not reduce drift" has no Lean statement.

The reactive schedule, and local liveness

  • A validator waits only until it holds the leader's block, then votes; the timeout is a fallback.
  • The vote round then takes at most drift + delivery + processing. When that sum is below the timeout, no timeout fires.
  • Every reliable validator decides from the blocks it holds, by an explicit time.

vote_or_wait, prompt_vote (LeanDag/Reactive/Basic.lean:96, 106); ReactiveM.cert_or_wait (LeanDag/Reactive/Mysticeti.lean:31); built_succ_le_of_fast (Basic.lean:166, D + δ + proc); built_succ_le_of_fast_gst (:220, Δ + δ + 2·proc); no_timeout_of_fast (:194), no_timeout_of_fast_gst (:243).

Local liveness: decided_local (LeanDag/Mysticeti/ViewPace.lean:507), commits_recur_local (:534), ReactiveM.decided_local (Reactive/Mysticeti.lean:119).

Witness ugrowReactive (LeanDagTest/Reactive/Model.lean:50): delay = 2, proc = 5, timeout = 9. The reactive schedule does not provide coverage (docstring); inclusion is preserved through the rotation (LeanDag/Reactive/MysticetiProperties.lean:96).

Chain quality

  • Coverage: the history of every committed block contains, at every round below it, blocks of at least |Correct| − f correct validators. No timing assumption is needed.
  • Inclusion: a correct validator's block is committed once a later slot it leads commits.
  • Coverage holds for every rule except Bluestreak. Inclusion holds for the seven rules with SelfParent and NoEquiv.
Uses: Quorate and CommitsCandidate (coverage); SelfParent, NoEquiv and LeaderCommits (inclusion).
Gives: lower bounds on which correct validators' blocks enter the ledger.

card_coveredAt_ge_of_decided (LeanDag/Properties/Arcs/Quality.lean:96); mem_history_of_decided_commit (:150); committed_of_correct_block (:195); chain_quality (:223).

Coverage instances: LeanDagTest/Quality/Generic.lean. Steelhead's coverage instance is not written; its inclusion is in liveness (LeanDag/Steelhead/Properties.lean:301).

The figure: slot 1 (round 3, leader 1) commits block 13 (ucens_slot1); its certificates lie at round 5, outside the drawn rounds.

Coverage does not give inclusion

Validators 0, 1, 2 reference only each other for six rounds; validator 3 is correct and no other validator references it. Each round of the commit has 2 correct creators, exactly the bound. None of validator 3's blocks enters the committed leader's history.

Ucens (LeanDagTest/Quality/Model.lean:312–405): Correct = {1, 2, 3}; ucens_slot1 (:339); missingAt Ucens 13 r = {3} (:345–347), of card f (:348); coveredAt … 13 1 = {1, 2} (:351); no block of 3 in slot 1's history (:364); block 7 not in the ledger (:393).

Validator 3's blocks reference its own previous block and two of the others; no block of validators 0, 1, 2 references validator 3.

Equivocation and exposure

  • Safety requires no restriction on equivocation; bounded storage does.
  • A creator is exposed in a block's history when the history holds two of its blocks in one round.
  • Rule: never reference a block whose creator is exposed in your own history.
  • This alone bounds a history, but with a constant that grows like f^f: one history can hold 2^e chains of one creator.
Uses: no property of the rule; only which blocks a validator accepts.
Gives: a bound on what a correct validator stores (next slide).

ExposedIn (LeanDag/DoS/Exposure.lean:43); DoSValid (:77); card_history_le' (LeanDag/DoS/Pedigree.lean:723: |H(b)| ≤ (n + (n − 1)·f^f)·(r + 1)).

Witness: udouble_four_chains (topsOf Udouble 41 1 = {1, 13, 14, 15}), udouble_exposed (exposedTo Udouble 41 = {1, 2}), udouble_dosValid (LeanDagTest/DoS/Doubling.lean:119, 122, 101). The figure: rows v0–v3 are Byzantine; the dark lines are paths from block 41 to validator 1's blocks 1, 13, 14, 15 (outlined red with validator 2's twins 27, 29). Block 39 is exposed to validator 1 but not to validator 2; block 41 holds both of validator 2's round-1 blocks 27 and 29.

Safety results restated under DoSValid without using it: LeanDagTest/DoS/SafetyUnderDoS.lean.

The novelty budget

  • Accept a block only if its history adds at most τ blocks you do not hold; reference only blocks you have accepted.
  • The rule is independent of a block's creator.
  • Storage then grows linearly: with C correct validators, a correct validator holds at most C·((1 + fτ)·n + 1 + f) blocks at round n. At C = 3, f = 1, τ = 3, round 9: 114 blocks.

UniformBudget (LeanDag/DoS/Novelty.lean:192); RefsAccepted (:452); dos_resistance (:729); dos_resistance_of_pace' (LeanDag/Mysticeti/PaceDelivery.lean:165).

After a round R, a correct block's novelty is at most f·κ + 1 (card_novelty_le_of_byzBudget, Novelty.lean:432).

The chart evaluates the bound of dos_resistance in the factored form of dos_resistance_of_pace', C·((1 + fτ)·n + 1 + f).

The cut

  • Each validator keeps a horizon G and discards every block below it. Validators do not agree on G.
  • Keep the blocks of rounds ≥ G and renumber round G as round 0, with no references. The result is again a valid DAG.
  • Slot d + k of the full DAG and slot k of the cut DAG have the same verdict.
Uses: Banded, Agree, and Law 1 of the support. Gives: the same verdicts and liveness after the cut, and constant storage (next slide).

BlockRecord.chop (LeanDag/Common/Record/Chop.lean:20); Slots.chop (LeanDag/GC/ChopDecided.lean:34); decided_chop_iff (LeanDag/Properties/Arcs/Record.lean:39, premise G ≤ slotRound d); decided_agree_chop (:46); decided_agree_horizons (LeanDag/Properties/Arcs/GC.lean:60); chop_chop (LeanDag/GC/Horizon.lean:57).

Uses Banded (through LocalTruncate), Agree, and Law 1 (live_of_truncates, LeanDag/Properties/Arcs/Liveness.lean:146).

Witness, LeanDagTest/GC/Chop.lean: chop Uexcl 2 (:46–49; block 8 at round 0 with no references); DirectCommit Uexcl 11 3 and DirectCommit (chop Uexcl 2) 11 1 (:60–61); the decided slot before and after (:72–84).

Storage is constant

With the horizon at most Λ rounds below the current round, a correct validator keeps at most C·(Λ + 1) + C·f + Λ·C·f·κ blocks, whatever the round. Here κ bounds the number of new blocks that accepting one Byzantine block adds to the store. At C = 3, f = 1, κ = 3, Λ = 5: 66 blocks.

card_retained_le (LeanDag/GC/Window.lean:189), under ByzBudget D κ, RefsAccepted D, G ≤ t ≤ G + Λ. C is the number of correct validators. At the slide's values: 3·6 + 3·1 + 5·3·1·3 = 18 + 3 + 45 = 66.

Joining from an attested base

  • A new validator adopts the round-G blocks that are reached from blocks of at least f + 1 distinct creators at a later round t.
  • One of those creators is correct, so every base block is attested by a correct validator. No signatures are needed.
  • It then copies a correct peer's blocks above G. Its verdicts equal those of any validator with the full history.

Base (LeanDag/GC/AttestedBase.lean:40); exists_correct_attester_of_mem_base (:55); bootstrap_agree (LeanDag/GC/Bootstrap.lean:169, needs m + 2 ≤ t); joinIds (:100).

Witness: Base Uexcl 4 1 = {5, 6, 7}, joinIds Dexcl 1 2 4 1 = {5, …, 10} (LeanDagTest/GC/Bootstrap.lean:150, 153); Base Utwin 1 0 = {1, 2, 3} with both equivocation halves excluded (LeanDagTest/GC/Chop.lean:139). In Uexcl, validator 0 equivocates at round 0 (blocks 0 and 4).

Choosing the lag

An equivocation whose two blocks both fall below the cut is no longer detected.

Safety: decided_agree_chop, decided_agree_horizons, bootstrap_agree. One round: viewUpto_subset_viewUpto_succ, pruned_subset_peer_store (LeanDag/GC/Horizon.lean:76, 94). Two rounds: accepted_mem_base (LeanDag/GC/Bootstrap.lean:44).

Forgotten equivocation: ¬ ExposedIn (chop Umerge 1) 9 0 (LeanDagTest/GC/Chop.lean:105); dosValid_chop (LeanDag/GC/Chop.lean:110).

(informal) A cut above an undecided slot leaves it undecided.

Crash recovery: the message

  • A validator v₁ crashed after its block B₁ and returns at round r. It cannot create a block: a valid block needs its own previous block one round below.
  • It sends one message: B₁, r, a donor validator v₂, and fresh identifiers.
  • Every receiver computes a filled block for v₁ at each missed round: the donor's references and payload at that round, plus a reference to v₁'s previous block.
Uses: Banded (through Persist), Agree, SkipsUnsupported, Law 1. Gives: v₁ producing again, with every earlier verdict unchanged.

GapData.hgap (LeanDag/SafeSkip/Data.lean:49); SkipData (:30–73); SkipMsg (LeanDag/SafeSkip/Basic.lean:52); SkipData.fillBlock (Data.lean:159); Integration.fill_refs_eq (LeanDag/Integration/CommonTarget.lean:74).

Witness ucrashMsg (LeanDagTest/SafeSkip/Model.lean:124, 178): v1 = 3, B1 = 3, donor line v2 = 1 (blocks 5, 9, 13, 17), fresh ids 4(N + 1) + k. The Lean example at :178 is the round-1 filled block of ucrashMsg 2 2, with references {3, 0, 1, 2}; the figure uses N = r = 4.

(informal) "Rebuilding costs one round trip per missed round".

What the fill guarantees

  1. The filled DAG is valid, and every old block is unchanged.
  2. v₁ has a block at every missed round, so it can produce again.
  3. A slot led by v₁ in the missed rounds is skipped at once, given a quorum one round above (the prompt skip). No later view can commit it.
  4. Every verdict reached before the fill agrees with every verdict after it.

skipFill, skipFill_block_old, skipFill_populatedOn (LeanDag/SafeSkip/Basic.lean:166, 171, 184).

Prompt skip: MysticetiProperties.decided_none_fresh (LeanDag/Mysticeti/Record.lean:188); generic Arcs.decided_none_of_novel, decided_none_of_novel_agree (LeanDag/Properties/Arcs/SafeSkip.lean:32, 87), using SkipsUnsupported, and for the second, Agree and Banded. Instances: Mysticeti, Odontoceti (LeanDag/Odontoceti/Record.lean:61), Hybrid (LeanDag/Hybrid/Record.lean:67), Hydrozoan (LeanDag/Integration/HydrozoanMechanisms.lean:79), Bluestreak (LeanDag/Bluestreak/Record.lean:314).

Verdicts: decided_fill_of_persist, decided_fill_agree_of_properties (LeanDag/Mysticeti/Record.lean:150, 159).

In this witness the schedule rrSlots places slots at rounds 3k, so no slot in rounds 1–4 is led by validator 3; the prompt skip is exhibited on Ucr (slide 85).

Jumping rounds

  • A validator's own blocks form a chain, so the donor's whole line is fixed by its top block.
  • The fill depends only on B₁, the donor's top block B₂, and the fresh identifiers. The message carries only these.
  • A receiver that holds B₂ holds the donor's whole line. After the one message, v₁ has a block at every round up to B₂'s round, so it can produce at the next.

line_eq_lineOf (LeanDag/SafeSkip/Jump.lean:174); skipFill_eq_of_core (:238); JumpMsg (:282), JumpMsg.denote (:345); lineOf_mem_view (:363); ucrashJump, ucrashJump_denote_eq (LeanDagTest/SafeSkip/Model.lean:250).

(informal) "Constant size": fresh is an identifier supply.

Limits of the fill

  • With a horizon Λ rounds below, recovery in one message works for outages of at most Λ rounds; for longer ones B₁ has been discarded.
  • No old block references a filled block, so v₁ is not covered in the rounds it missed.
  • The storage rule must be re-checked; with a donor line whose blocks all reach B₁, and v₁ not equivocating, it is one reachability check per round.
  • If the donor line is taken from blocks every receiver already holds, nothing else needs to be sent.

outage_bounded_by_lag (LeanDag/Integration/Retention.lean:174), anchor_pruned (:27). not_synchronisedOn_skipFill, synchronisedOn_skipFill_of_notMem (LeanDag/Integration/Coverage.lean:37, 52).

history_B1_subset_fill, dosValid_skipFill_of_covered (LeanDag/Integration/Exposure.lean:48, 170). fill_refs_available (LeanDag/Integration/CommonTarget.lean:63; it covers the copied references, not the self-reference).

Re-genesis: recovering after a long outage

  • If all of v₁'s blocks are below the horizon, its chain of own blocks cannot be continued.
  • Each validator adds a round-0 block for v₁, with no references, to its cut DAG. This needs no exception to the self-parent rule.
  • Procedure: (1) join from the attested base to read; (2) re-genesis to write; (3) one fill message from the genesis block to the current round.
  • While a quorum still produces blocks, at most f validators can be in this state at once.
Uses: Banded, Agree, Law 1, and the attested base (slide 78). Gives: a validator back in production after any outage.

no_blocks_of_no_genesis, severed_of_pruned_anchor (LeanDag/Integration/Retention.lean:44, 65); BlockRecord.addGenesis (LeanDag/Common/Record/Genesis.lean:20); addGenesis_of_severed (LeanDag/Integration/ReGenesis.lean:95); recoveryMsg, hB1uniq_of_addGenesis, rejoin_populated (ReGenesis.lean); card_severed_le (LeanDag/Integration/Margin.lean:40).

Witness: Ucut, ucut_severed, Uregen, urecover (LeanDagTest/Integration/Model.lean:102–160). The filled block 1001 copies the references of the donor's block 9 and adds 999. The genesis block is valid only in a DAG cut at G or above.

(informal) "Derived locally, not transmitted": regenesis_converges proves only that a later cut removes it.

The chain fill (Bluestreak)

  • Copying a donor's references would attribute to v₁ claims it never made.
  • Each filled block references only v₁'s previous block and carries no tag and no claim. The message is (v₁, B₁, r); no donor.
  • Verdicts do not change: slot 2 is committed and slot 3 skipped, before and after.
Uses: the same properties as the fill, and Bluestreak's claim discipline.
Gives: recovery for a rule whose blocks carry claims.

GapData.chainBlock (LeanDag/SafeSkip/Data.lean:91); chainFill (LeanDag/Bluestreak/Record.lean:174); disciplined_chainFill (:231).

LeanDagTest/Bluestreak/Recovery.lean: rcFaults (:28, validator 0 Byzantine), rcGap (:73, v1 = 3, B1 = 7, r = 3), blocks 102, 103 (:93), Ucr_slot2, Ufill_slot2, Ucr_slot3, Ufill_slot3, prompt skip (:134–150). Validator 3 is correct and silent from round 2; slot 3 is led by validator 3.

(informal) The motivation in the first bullet.

Every mechanism is one relation

Each mechanism relates the DAG it reads to the DAG it writes: the same blocks from a settling round on, renumbered by G rounds, with the same creators and payloads, and the same references strictly above the settling round.

  • A cut is such a relation; so are a fill and a re-genesis (with G = 0).
  • A sequence of them is again one.
Uses: Banded, Agree, Law 1.
Gives: safety and liveness for any combination of cuts, fills and re-geneses (next slide).

A cut, a fill and a re-genesis are each a relation of this one form; a sequence of them is again one, settling at the later of the settling rounds. The figure: a fill of rounds 6–10 followed by a cut at G = 15; stack_core settles at max (r + 1, G), here 15.

RebasedAbove (LeanDag/Properties/Carrier.lean:68, references :81); Truncates (LeanDag/Properties/Truncate.lean:43); Sustains (LeanDag/Properties/Sustain.lean:89); Stack, Stack.rebased (LeanDag/Properties/Arcs/Stack.lean:32, 40); stack_core (LeanDag/Integration/StackRules.lean:42).

Safe and live across any stack

From Banded, Agree and Law 1: across any stack, verdicts above the settling round are preserved, views agree, and the liveness precondition is preserved.
The cut, fill and re-genesis are each built once, and serve ten of the eleven rules.

Stack.safe_and_live (Stack.lean:109). onRecord instances for Nemo, Mysticeti, Odontoceti, Hybrid, FinWhale, Hydrozoan, Optimal-Hydrozoan, Bluestreak, Mahi-Mahi, Async BlueBottle; none for Steelhead. Steelhead's cut cell is its own localTruncate (LeanDag/Steelhead/Properties.lean:146).

Leaders chosen from the committed prefix

  • A fixed schedule may continue to name a crashed leader.
  • A configuration fixes the leaders of each round and an interval.
  • It decides up to its anchor (the first committed slot more than one interval past its start), but outputs only up to its boundary.
  • The next configuration is computed from the anchor's history and the verdicts just output.
Uses: Agree (safety); Law 2 and Indirect (liveness).
Gives: a schedule every validator computes the same way.

Configuration 0 starts at round 0 with its boundary at round 1; its anchor is slot 3 at round 3. Its verdicts at slots 1, 2, 3 are block 5, skip, block 15; its output is [5]. Configurations 1 and 2 decide slot 3 again as 15, and configuration 2 outputs [15].

Barnacle.Config (LeanDag/Barnacle/Config.lean:28); Run.anchor_commits, anchor_least (LeanDag/Barnacle/Model/Run.lean:90–96); Run.rangeLedger (:139); Boundary.atThreshold (LeanDag/Barnacle/Model/Rule.lean:204). segRun (LeanDagTest/Adaptive/Asynchronous.lean:46–113, 121). (informal) The crashed-leader motivation.

Safe for every anchored score

  • Two validators that start from the same configuration agree on every configuration and every verdict.
  • No timing, fairness or window assumption, and any score, provided the update reads the view only through the anchor's history.
  • For liveness the score must continue to assign reliable validators runs of consecutive slots.

Barnacle.Agreement.holds (LeanDag/Barnacle/Agreement/Proof.lean:16; Statement.lean:47–90): hypotheses Properties.Agree and Anchored R upd. Score.rule_anchored, Adaptive.score_safe (LeanDag/Adaptive/Headline.lean:55); Adaptive.score_live (:102); headsRun_of_cycle_weighted (LeanDag/Barnacle/Helpers/Heads.lean:297).

What a score may read

  • A score that reads only the anchor's history is unaffected by crash recovery.
  • Under garbage collection the score must read verdicts relative to the configuration: a score that names an absolute slot number gives different answers before and after a cut.

UpdStable (LeanDag/Adaptive/Helpers/Mechanisms.lean:140), Score.stable_of_readsHistory, swapScore_stable; HorizonStable (LeanDag/Adaptive/Helpers/Chop.lean:86), horizonStable_relabel (:140); commitScore_not_horizonStable (LeanDagTest/Adaptive/Asynchronous.lean:226).

The adaptive leader count

More leaders per round lower latency, but one slow leader delays every later slot. At each anchor:

  1. count the directly committed slots in the anchor's history;
  2. healthy if num · expected ≤ den · observed;
  3. healthy: one more leader; unhealthy: 2^backoff fewer, between 1 and maxLeaders; the backoff resets when healthy and grows otherwise.
Uses: Agree, CommitsCandidate, CommitsDirect (the count reads direct commits).
Gives: a leader count every validator computes the same way.

The chart: five windows (healthy, healthy, unhealthy, unhealthy, healthy) take the count 1 → 2 → 3 → 2 → 1 → 2, backoff 0, 0, 0, 1, 2, maxLeaders = 4. The inset: on Usun, configuration 0 closes at anchor 21 (slot 5) with observed = 2 = expected, and configuration 1 has two leaders per round after round 5.

observed (LeanDag/Barnacle/Model/Window.lean); Aimd.rule, Aimd.count (LeanDag/Barnacle/Aimd/Rule.lean). expected is C.cum (r + 1 − waveLength) − C.cum (r − interval); at uniform width m and r ≥ interval it is (interval − waveLength + 1)·m (checked by decide at m = 2, interval = 4, waveLength = 3: 4). Usun (LeanDagTest/Barnacle/Agreement.lean:100). The plotted sequence is checked by decide at bnP (maxLeaders = 4; LeanDagTest/Barnacle/Agreement.lean:263). (informal) The latency motivation.

The leader count: findings

  • Safety holds for any anchored update rule, AIMD included.
  • If the interval is shorter than the wave, the expected count is 0, the test always passes, and the count increases at every anchor.
  • Liveness under several leaders per round is proved for round-robin when waveLength · slack + 1 ≤ n.

Barnacle.Agreement.holds (as slide 89); Healthy.Vacuous (LeanDag/Barnacle/Healthy/Statement.lean); Live.runsExist_roundRobin (LeanDag/Barnacle/Live/Proof.lean:27). Base-rule witnesses: LeanDagTest/Barnacle/Rules (Hydrozoan, Mysticeti, Nemo, Odontoceti, Optimal-Hydrozoan, Orcaella).

Checkpoints

  • Correct online validators sign the checkpoint their deterministic state machine reaches after each commit in their own view, and witness certificates for what they signed.
  • A checkpoint certificate is at least q signatures on one proposal; a finality certificate is at least q witnesses of one.
  • Two checkpoint certificates at one epoch and height agree.
  • A correctly led slot, with production and certification, is finalised.
  • At an epoch change, the highest validated checkpoint becomes the next epoch's genesis.
Uses: Agree, CommitsCandidate, Law 2.
Gives: finalised application state, and its recovery across epochs.

SigningRule.proposes, .witnesses (LeanDag/Checkpoint/CommitSpec.lean:66); CheckpointQC, FinalityQC (LeanDag/Checkpoint/BaseSpec.lean:117, 169); checkpointQC_eq_of_same_height (LeanDag/Checkpoint/SafetyProofs.lean:89); liveCommitFinalized (LeanDag/Checkpoint/CommitProofs.lean:88); IsSelected, EpochTransition (LeanDag/Checkpoint/RecoverySpec.lean). Safety is within one epoch (checkpointQC_prefix). Instances: LeanDag/Integration/HybridCheckpoint.lean, LeanDag/Integration/BarnacleCheckpoint.lean.

Red Snapper: a fast path for owned objects

  • Validators state a stance on each object version inside their ordinary blocks; certificates for transactions, skips and unlocks are read from the DAG.
  • At n ≥ 3f + 1, uncontested transactions are decided from the DAG; conflicts are resolved at a committed anchor.
  • At n ≥ 5f + 1, a validator may change its vote on 2f + 1 opposing votes, coordinated by a coin.
  • Among any n − f votes one side reaches 2f + 1 exactly when n ≥ 5f + 1. The 5f + 1 certificate lemmas themselves need only n ≥ 3f + 1.
Uses: only the committed anchor sequence of the underlying consensus.
Gives: commits of owned-object transactions without waiting for consensus, except under conflict.

Both panels: n = 4, validator 0 Byzantine (no blocks after round 0). Left, ULive: block 4 (validator 1) carries and ACKs tx 0; rounds 2–3 every correct block stands at ack 0; FastQuorumAt ULive 3 0, verdict finalized with an empty anchor sequence. Right, UTri: the two conflicting transactions 0 and 1 on object 0, every correct block declares ⊥; each correct round-3 block is an unlock certificate (IsUnlockCert UTri 10 0, 12 0); anchor 12 releases the object and both transactions are dropped.

Faults.card_validators (LeanDag/RedSnapper/Model/Faults.lean:52); Uncontested, ConflictResolution (LeanDag/RedSnapper/); Revocation.ExposureAtQuorum (LeanDag/RedSnapper/Revocation/Statement.lean:115: half ≤ (quorum + 1)/2 ↔ 5f + 1 ≤ n); FullCertSafety (LeanDag/RedSnapper/Five/FullCertSafety/Statement.lean:86, over Faults, under MoveDiscipline). Witnesses ULive, UTri (LeanDagTest/RedSnapper/Liveness.lean:82, 162).

Open work

  • Adaptive leaders are proved generically; no rule has its own instance yet, and no score that moves more than one slot per validator is shown live.
  • Steelhead: fill, re-genesis, and the coverage half of chain quality.
  • Barbouni (proposed): change the schedule only at verdicts already decided.
  • Checkpoints: the broadcast algorithm is assumed, not modelled.

Generic adaptive liveness: liveOfAnchored (LeanDag/Barnacle/Model/Anchored.lean:70); Timed.descent_of_support (LeanDag/Timed/Coverage.lean:189), applied at 9 rules. swapScore and commitScore are live as permutations (liveOn_of_permuted). Steelhead has no onRecord. AuthenticatedBroadcast (LeanDag/Checkpoint/RecoverySpec.lean:29) is an assumed contract. (informal) Barbouni is in docs/barbouni.md only.

The development

  • LeanDag/Common/: blocks, the decision relation, ledgers.
  • LeanDag/Mysticeti/, LeanDag/Nemo/, …: one directory per rule.
  • LeanDag/Properties/: the properties and the safety and liveness headlines.
  • LeanDag/GC/, SafeSkip/, Reactive/, DoS/, Adaptive/, Barnacle/, Checkpoint/, Integration/: the mechanisms.
  • LeanDagTest/: every witness in this deck.
  • docs/report.md: the full written account.

lake build checks the library and the witnesses; every headline theorem's axioms are printed in the test files and are Lean's standard three (propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound).

Summary

  • One decision relation; eleven rules proved, two refuted.
  • Four properties and a support per rule; every mechanism proved once against them.
  • Safety with no network assumption; liveness from view convergence.
